items.note: 4B oval mass with partly indistinct margins, fibroadenoma at the same site. Concordant; a cautious flag on the margins is acceptable
flags: A fibroadenoma is a specific benign diagnosis and the shape is oval, but the mass has partly indistinct margins and internal vascularity at BI-RADS 4B, so the radiologist should decide whether it fully explains the finding.
items.summary: Left breast 1 o'clock, 1.6 cm oval hypoechoic mass with partly indistinct margins, BI-RADS 4B. Biopsy of the same site (left, 1 o'clock) shows fibroadenoma, negative for atypia and malignancy. Side and location agree, but the indistinct margins raise the question of whether a benign result explains the finding. The radiologist should decide on concordance.

items.note: 4C spiculated mass at 12 o'clock, fibrocystic change at 10 o'clock. Nonspecific benign result does not explain a spiculated mass, and the location differs
flags: Benign fibrocystic change does not specifically explain a spiculated, irregular, shadowing BI-RADS 4C mass, so sampling error or a missed target is possible.
The biopsy site is 10 o'clock, but the imaging mass is at 12 o'clock, so the biopsy may not have sampled the target lesion.
items.summary: Right breast 1.4 cm irregular, spiculated, shadowing mass, BI-RADS 4C, was biopsied. Pathology shows benign fibrocystic change with no carcinoma, which does not specifically explain a highly suspicious finding. The pathology site (10 o'clock) also differs from the imaging location (12 o'clock), so this is a possible mismatch for radiologist review.

items.note: BI-RADS 5 spiculated mass, invasive lobular carcinoma at the same site
flags: The imaging report recommended biopsy of the left axillary lymph node as well, but the pathology report only lists the breast specimen, so the node has no pathology result here.
The specimen is labeled as repeat sampling, but the imaging report describes no earlier biopsy, so the prior sampling is unexplained.
items.summary: Left breast 2 o'clock 2.8 cm irregular spiculated mass, BI-RADS 5, with pathology showing invasive lobular carcinoma, grade 2. Cancer in a highly suspicious mass is concordant, and side and clock position agree. The axillary node has no pathology result in this report, and the "repeat sampling" label has no matching prior biopsy in the imaging report.

items.note: 4A oval mass with indistinct margins, fibroadenoma at the same site
flags: The mass is described with indistinct margins, which is a suspicious feature and less typical for a fibroadenoma, so the radiologist may want to confirm that the result explains the finding.
items.summary: The biopsied finding is a 1.1 cm oval hypoechoic mass in the right breast at 10 o'clock, with indistinct margins and BI-RADS 4A. Pathology from the same site shows fibroadenoma with no atypia or malignancy, which is a specific benign diagnosis that reasonably fits an oval mass and a low-suspicion category. Breast and location agree. The indistinct margins are the one feature the radiologist may want to weigh.

items.note: 4C spiculated mass, invasive ductal carcinoma at the same site

items.summary: Imaging shows a suspicious 1.6 cm left breast mass (BI-RADS 4B), and pathology shows invasive ductal carcinoma with DCIS, which would fit a suspicious mass. items.summary: Imaging shows a 1.1 cm oval hypoechoic right breast mass with indistinct margins, BI-RADS 4A. flags: The pathology specimen is labeled right breast, but the imaging finding and biopsy recommendation are for the left breast.

items.summary: The imaging describes a suspicious 1.2 cm left breast mass with angular margins at 6 o'clock (BI-RADS 4), but the pathology specimen is labeled right breast, 2 o'clock, stereotactic biopsy. The side, location and biopsy method all differ, so the specimen may not be from the imaged lesion. Even if the sample were correct, ADH would be a limited explanation for a suspicious mass.

items.note: Addendum upgraded a mass to 4A for indistinct margins, fibroadenoma at the same site
flags: The mass was re-read as having indistinct margins, which is a suspicious feature, while a fibroadenoma usually presents as a circumscribed mass, so the benign result may not fully explain the finding.
items.summary: Right breast 8 o'clock mass, re-read as indistinct margins and BI-RADS 4A. Biopsy shows fibroadenoma with myxoid stroma, no atypia or malignancy, from the same breast and location. items.note: BI-RADS 5 with a benign result, and the location differs. The rules flag BI-RADS 5 plus benign regardless, but Claude should also catch it

items.summary: A BI-RADS 5, 2.8 cm irregular spiculated left breast mass at 2 o'clock was biopsied, and pathology shows fat necrosis negative for malignancy. This is a possible mismatch for radiologist review.

items.note: Right 4C spiculated mass, left LCIS. Side differs and LCIS does not form a spiculated mass

Classic LCIS without invasive carcinoma does not clearly explain a spiculated, irregular, shadowing BI-RADS 4C mass.
items.summary: The imaging finding is a suspicious 1.4 cm irregular spiculated right breast mass at 12 o'clock, BI-RADS 4C. The pathology specimen is labeled left breast 4 o'clock and shows classic LCIS without invasive carcinoma. The side and location differ, and the diagnosis does not clearly explain the finding, so this is a possible mismatch for radiologist review.

items.note: A screening recall with no biopsied finding described, paired with a pathology report. Not enough to compare
flags: The biopsy was taken from the left breast, but the imaging finding is in the right breast and the left breast was unremarkable.

items.summary: The imaging report describes a possible 9 mm right breast focal asymmetry (BI-RADS 0, needs additional imaging) with an unremarkable left breast. The pathology is a benign fibroadenoma from a left breast 1 o'clock biopsy. The laterality and location differ, so this biopsy may not correspond to the imaging finding.
